say: Goal first. "Premium" means nothing until it is pinned to dimensions and values; then three screens in that vocabulary, and one example of what it is not.
Old-school e-banking: dense tables, many colours, tiny type. This is the not-this.
The Apple Card: titanium white, almost nothing printed on it. Restraint as luxury.
The Apple Card's ground: one quiet material, nothing printed on it.
The old e-banking screen fails the same dimension: no hierarchy at all.
The vocabulary, pinned from the references: ground, ornament, hierarchy, type, colour, density - each with a value, and what it is not.
Card detail, drawn from the home screen: same ground, same serif hero, the card as the one ornament.
The not-this, made precise: the same screen with only ornament turned up.
Laying out the sheet: the vocabulary first, then the three screens, then what premium is not.
Fair: the old e-banking screen is a different design. The not-this that matters is our own screen pushed one dimension too far, so it stays alone.
The not-this row is marked as a contrast.
Checking the sheet: the three screens must be one design; the not-this is set apart.
